nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression model used for normative modeling of brain development.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: A model of brain development as a function of age and sex was created by training a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model, which is a nonparametric nonlinear regression technique with additive Gaussian noise, on a sample of n = 129 and n = 127 (77 cases, Table 1, online Supplementary Fig. S3 for an age distribution) to predict brain function and structure, respectively
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Constructing normative models of brain structure and function

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Task-fMRI GLM regression coefficient images from the emotion matching task; anatomical Jacobian determinants of deformation fields.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: First, normative modeling to map deviations from the typical age-related pattern at the level of the individual of (i) activity during emotion matching and (ii) of anatomical images derived from DBD cases ( n = 77) and controls ( n = 52) aged 8 -18 years from the EU-funded Aggressotype and MATRICS consortia. ... The GLM regression coefficient images and the Z images (deviation images) of the normative model of the 140 participants were visually inspected ... We decided to take the nonlinear Jacobian determinants as feature for the normative model given that they quantify the overall degree of tissue expansion or contraction required to match each image to the population template.
